ei.title: The Unexpected Accuracy of First Impressions
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.

questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found (A)[doubt / evidence] that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they (B)[recognize / forget] the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the (C)[inferior / superior] performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① doubt — recognize — superior: (A) doubt(의심)는 Dunning이 '증거(evidence)'를 발견했다는 맥락과 다름
❌ ② evidence — forget — superior: (B) forget(잊다)은 사람을 '알아본다(recognize)'는 맥락과 반대
✅ ③ evidence — recognize — superior: Dunning은 증거(evidence)를 발견했고, 사람을 알아보는(recognize) 이유를 설명 못 할 때 정확하며, 무의식적 직감이 더 우수한(superior) 수행을 보인다는 맥락에 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ evidence — recognize — inferior: (C) inferior(열등한)는 '우수한(superior)'과 반대
det.tip: found evidence / why they recognize the person / the superior performance

det.analysis:
❌ ① reaction(반응): 즉각적 반응으로 신중한 숙고와 반대

✅ ② deliberation: 결정 전에 오래 신중히 생각하는 과정으로 영영 정의와 일치 ←정답

❌ ③ impression(인상): 받은 느낌이지 숙고 과정이 아님

❌ ④ guess(추측): 근거 없는 짐작으로 신중한 숙고와 반대
det.tip: deliberation = 숙고. long and careful thinking before a decision이 핵심

questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning __________ (conduct) experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence of inaccurate identification.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 뒤에 and로 연결되는 동사 found(과거)와 병렬을 이루므로 과거시제가 필요. 과거의 실험을 서술하므로 conduct의 과거형 conducted가 적절. conduct → conducted
det.tip: and found(과거)와 병렬 → conducted(과거시제)

questions.passage: That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the __________ (deliberate), reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 빈칸은 뒤의 명사구 'reasoned self-narrative'를 수식하는 형용사 자리. reasoned와 콤마로 병렬되는 형용사가 필요하므로 deliberate의 형용사형 deliberative(숙고하는/신중한)가 적절. deliberate → deliberative
det.tip: deliberate(동사/형용사) → deliberative(형용사: 신중한). the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative

questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very __________ can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① final verdict(최종 판결): 즉각적 반응을 다루는 맥락과 다름

❌ ② careful analysis(신중한 분석): 본문은 신중한 분석보다 직감을 강조하므로 반대

✅ ③ first impression: 'That very __________ can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative'에서 즉각적·직감적 반응을 가리키는 '첫인상(first impression)'이 신중한 서술보다 더 정확할 수 있다는 맥락 ←정답

❌ ④ group opinion(집단 의견): 개인의 즉각적 반응 맥락과 무관
det.tip: That very first impression = 바로 그 첫인상 (즉각적 직감)

questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical __________ justifications for a decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① step-by-step: 'compared to logical __________ justifications for a decision'에서 무의식적 직감과 대비되는, 논리적으로 '단계별(step-by-step)' 정당화라는 맥락. 직감 대 논리적 추론의 대비가 단서 ←정답

❌ ② last-minute(막판의): 논리적 추론 과정 맥락과 부적절

❌ ③ well-known(잘 알려진): 문맥과 무관

❌ ④ large-scale(대규모의): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: logical step-by-step justifications = 논리적 단계별 정당화
